eval.eval_cmd: python -m seg.evaluate --model peaknet_baseline --config configs/peaknet_baseline_pw.yaml --ckpt /sdf/data/lcls/ds/prj/prjcwang31/results/peaknet-seg-sprint/checkpoints/h2/pk_d/best.pt --split test --workers 8 --save-overlays OUT --n-overlays 4 --out test_metrics.json  (config eval.val_thr -> val-picked threshold)

notes: Model code is upstream PeakNet unchanged (peaknet.modeling.convnextv2_bifpn_net.PeakNet, base.yaml architecture); only the head is 1 class. Trained with the shared seg/train.py: 512 crops (4 per image, 80% centred on a peak), rot90/flip + gain jitter, AdamW wd .05, cosine, focal(alpha .75, gamma 2) x10 + dice, bf16 AMP, best checkpoint by val peak F1 on 200 val images. Three stages, each a fine-tune of the last: pk_a (from scratch, log1p + per-image standardisation, saturated 65535 pixels only clamped): val peak F1 .571 @3k, precision .40 (fires on the unlabelled saturated runs along panel edges). pk_b (+ saturated pixels -> 0, lr 3e-4, 55 min): val .820, test .805 (thr .999), was the first landed result. pk_d (this result; + pointwise log input norm seg.infer.norm_log instead of per-image standardisation, h5's finding; lr 1.5e-4, 50 min): val .877 @1k, .889 @2k, .901 @4k (best.pt), .895 @6k. Test threshold .99 picked on every 3rd val image (488) over .2-.999, then all 1529 test images at that threshold: peak F1 .895 (P .894 R .896), pixel IoU .307. Dead ends: patch_size 2 + learned ConvTranspose upsampler (h1 pk_p2, val .075, checkerboard speckle); pk_c lower lr + focal alpha .5 (no gain over pk_b). Weakness: the 1/4-res head (bilinear 4x upsample) limits pixel IoU on 1-2 px peaks.
